items.followUp: Describe the structure and functions of the cell wall, with a labelled diagram.

rubric.why: The bilayer is the basic structure of the cell membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the membrane consists of a phospholipid bilayer.

rubric.why: Proteins embedded in the bilayer are an important part of the membrane structure.
rubric.description: State that proteins are embedded in the bilayer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying embedded membrane proteins.

rubric.why: The membrane regulates the exchange of substances with the cell’s surroundings.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.

rubric.why: The diagram should show and label the main parts of the bilayer in their correct arrangement.
rubric.description: Provide a recognisable labelled membrane diagram.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a diagram showing outward-facing heads, inward-facing tails and a membrane protein, with these parts labelled.

modelAnswer: The cell membrane is a thin, flexible boundary that surrounds the cytoplasm and separates it from the external environment.
It consists mainly of a phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it.
The hydrophilic heads face the watery environments, while the hydrophobic tails face inward.
The membrane is selectively permeable and controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.

Diagram construction: draw two rows of phospholipids with the hydrophilic heads facing outward and the hydrophobic tails facing inward; add a protein embedded in the bilayer; label the hydrophilic heads, hydrophobic tails, protein and phospholipid bilayer. No scale is required.

items.followUp: Define classification and write the taxonomic hierarchy from kingdom to order, describing each level.

rubric.why: The definition must identify the hierarchy as a ranked arrangement of classification groups.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing organisms as arranged into ranked or successive taxonomic groups.

rubric.why: The requested ranks must be given in the correct order.
rubric.description: List the hierarchy from kingdom to family.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the complete correct sequence; award 1 mark for a mostly correct sequence with one omission or order error.

rubric.why: This describes the broadest rank and the group it contains.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a kingdom contains phyla or is the broadest rank containing phyla.

rubric.why: These relationships describe how the remaining requested ranks group into increasingly specific taxa.
rubric.description: Describe the grouping relationships from phylum through family.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for accurately describing the successive grouping relationships, including that a family contains related genera.

modelAnswer: A taxonomic hierarchy is the arrangement of organisms into successive, ranked groups called taxa, from broad groups to increasingly specific ones.
Kingdom is the broadest rank and contains related phyla.
A phylum contains related classes.
A class contains related orders.
An order contains related families.
A family contains related genera.

items.followUp: Explain the causes and symptoms of diarrhoea and constipation, and state how each can be managed.

rubric.why: Frequent loose or watery stools are the defining feature of diarrhoea.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the frequent passage of loose or watery stools.

rubric.why: Diarrhoea can cause loss of body water and salts, leading to dehydration.
rubric.description: State an important effect of diarrhoea.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning loss of water and salts or the risk of dehydration.

rubric.why: Constipation involves hard stools or difficulty passing them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying hard, dry stools or difficulty in passing stools.

rubric.why: A peptic ulcer is damage to the lining of the gut.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an ulcer as a sore or erosion in the stomach or intestinal lining.

rubric.why: Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying inflammation of the appendix.

modelAnswer: Diarrhoea is the frequent passage of loose, watery stools. It causes excessive loss of water and salts and may lead to dehydration.
Constipation is the difficult passage of hard, dry stools, often due to slow movement of faeces through the large intestine.
A peptic ulcer is a sore or erosion in the lining of the stomach or intestine; it may cause pain and bleeding.
Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix and commonly causes abdominal pain.

items.followUp: Define guttation and explain how humidity, temperature and wind affect transpiration.

rubric.why: The definition identifies water-vapour loss from the above-ground parts of a plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining transpiration as loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant.

rubric.why: Higher temperature generally increases evaporation and transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that higher temperature generally increases the rate of transpiration.

rubric.why: High humidity reduces the water-vapour concentration difference between the leaf and air.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that higher humidity decreases the rate of transpiration.

rubric.why: Wind carries away moist air around the leaves and generally increases water loss.
rubric.description: State the effect of wind or air movement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that wind generally increases transpiration, for example by carrying away moist air.

modelAnswer: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mainly through the stomata of leaves.
Higher temperature generally increases the rate of transpiration by increasing evaporation.
High humidity decreases the rate because the difference in water-vapour concentration between the leaf and air is smaller.
Wind generally increases the rate by carrying away moist air around the leaves.

items.followUp: Define genetics and state what it studies.

rubric.why: Cell biology is a branch of biology.
rubric.description: Identify cell biology as a branch of biology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cell biology is a branch of biology.

rubric.why: The definition should identify cells and their structure and functions as its subject.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it studies cells, including their structure and functions.

modelAnswer: Cell biology is the branch of biology that studies cells, including their structure and functions.
